about: THE BUILD'S GRAPH (kb/Work PB5207, PB5218, PB5231; scripts/buildgraph.py). Each target has a KIND: a `test` target is a test assembly, which records a PASS; a `generated` target is a Python command that writes declared OUTPUTS into a directory of the worktree's own and records their DIGEST. Each declares its INPUTS (path patterns, each naming its reader), its exclusions (each naming why), the FACETS its key covers (all of `facets` unless it names fewer) and the targets it DEPENDS on. A target's key is a digest of its facets, the OUTPUT DIGEST of each dependency (never the dependency's inputs) and the git blob ids of the tracked paths its inputs match, less its exclusions; its record is stored once per target and key in the one store every worktree shares. An input missed here is a FALSE GREEN: the BUILD TARGETS audit (`python scripts/buildgraph.py check`) fails when a test source of an assembly names a repository path outside its target's inputs, and every run of a generated target is traced and refused when it reads outside its inputs. The test targets' order is the gate's host start order, the longest population first; scripts/test_population.py GATED_ASSEMBLIES reads the test assemblies from here (kb/Work PB5230).

conformance-suite.about: The conformance suite's manifests: conformance-suite/harness/generate.py, the one reader of the test headers, writes <edition>/manifest.json and wiseowl/manifest.json. It refuses a test that names a rule the inventory lacks, so the inventory is ITS input; conformance depends on its OUTPUT, so a records-only change that leaves the manifests byte-identical leaves conformance up to date (kb/Work PB5231). The inputs were derived by reading the generator and by a traced run of `generate.py --out` (kb/Work PB5218, PB5231), and every gate's run of it is traced again.
